USD.catalyst: The US Dollar Index trades near 99.16, hovering below its 20-day moving average of 99.38 and 50-day moving average of 100.22 while finding support above its 200-day moving average of 99.14. Resilient US economic growth and hawkish Federal Reserve expectations have anchored the dollar, with market participants pricing in an increased likelihood of a policy rate hike as target rates sit at 3.75%. Heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and WTI crude holding above $90.50 per barrel have maintained safe-haven demand for American assets. Meanwhile, short-term rate differentials favor the dollar, as OIS SOFR pricing at 3.66% offers a clear yield advantage against major peers like the euro and yen.

GBP.catalyst: The British pound remains supported by persistent Bank of England rate-hike expectations after monetary policy committee member Huw Pill advocated raising the bank rate to 4.00% to head off lingering inflationary pressures. While money market pricing reflects ongoing bets on additional tightening in 2026, economists polled by Reuters anticipate borrowing costs will remain unchanged through the end of the year. From a technical perspective, sterling trades above its 50-day moving average of 1.3456 and 200-day moving average of 1.3447, though it remains capped below its 20-day moving average of 1.3555. Traders are now monitoring upcoming UK macroeconomic releases and central bank testimony to gauge whether near-term economic growth can sustain hawkish policy guidance.

EUR.catalyst: The euro trades comfortably above $1.1500, supported by expectations that the European Central Bank will deliver a rate increase at its upcoming September policy meeting. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde signaled that inflation is projected to remain well above target until the first half of 2027, highlighting risks from renewed energy supply disruptions. While the ECB’s deposit rate sits at 2.40%, swaps markets have priced in nearly two interest rate hikes for 2026 amid ongoing energy price shocks. On the daily technical structure, the euro holds above its 20-day moving average of 1.1611 and 50-day moving average of 1.1512, though it faces overhead resistance near its 200-day moving average at 1.1638.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen has posted broad daily gains against G10 counterpart currencies as elevated intervention concerns and hawkish Bank of Japan chatter fuel long positioning. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Markets are focused on the central bank's upcoming September 17–18 policy meeting, where hawkish BOJ officials are expected to push for further rate hikes as their terms end next year. Despite a persistent policy rate gap with the Federal Reserve, the yen trades below its daily 20-day moving average of 158.96 and 200-day moving average of 158.45 against the dollar as carry-trade unwinding accelerates.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar shows steady strength across G10 crosses, backed by expectations that the RBA holds at 4.35%. Institutional demand remains firm, with leveraged funds holding a net long AUD position of +50,250 contracts, representing the 94th percentile of its 52-week distribution. Solid Chinese macroeconomic activity targeting 4.6% growth has provided additional tailwinds for Australian commodity exports. Technically, the Australian currency trades above its 20-day moving average of 0.7135, 50-day moving average of 0.7041, and 200-day moving average of 0.6988 against the US dollar, with market participants anticipating the RBA's next monetary policy decision.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar remains under pressure, weighed down by weak domestic labor data that showed wage growth slowing to 2.0%, reinforcing the Bank of Canada's decision to hold its overnight rate at 2.25%. Fresh trade friction with the US has further dimmed the outlook after President Donald Trump criticized currency valuation imbalances between the two nations. Higher crude oil prices have offered minimal support to the commodity-linked currency as monetary policy divergence favors the US dollar. In currency-level market structure, the Canadian dollar trades above its 200-day moving average of 1.3833 against the greenback, but below its 20-day moving average of 1.3861 and 50-day moving average of 1.4004.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc has softened against major peers following a neutral policy stance from the Swiss National Bank, despite a recent CPI print showing inflation ticking up to 0.8% year-on-year. Although energy prices drove much of the unexpected inflation surge, analysts note that the SNB remains reluctant to adjust interest rates, reducing the franc's yield appeal across carry trades. Market commentary from institutions including UBS indicates that low FX volatility has diminished the franc's typical safe-haven premium. Against the US dollar, the franc trades above its 20-day moving average of 0.8075, 50-day moving average of 0.8087, and 200-day moving average of 0.7932.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar trades with a slight soft tilt as market participants weigh local monetary policy guidance against global risk sentiment. Reserve Bank of New Zealand Assistant Governor Karen Silk signaled that a rate hike is more likely to occur at the December policy meeting than in October, even after Q2 inflation rose to a two-year high of 4.1% year-on-year. The currency remains sensitive to shifting Federal Reserve rate expectations and geopolitical developments in the Middle East. Against the US dollar, the kiwi sits below its 20-day moving average of 0.5910, but maintains a position above its 50-day moving average of 0.5839 and 200-day moving average of 0.5855.

Settlement of Norwegian krone foreign exchange transactions continues to run through the Scandinavian Cash Pool and CLS facilities at Norges Bank to secure bank liquidity. On daily technical metrics against the US dollar, the krone trades below its 20-day moving average of 9.370, 50-day moving average of 9.554, and 200-day moving average of 9.627.

Low inflation estimates and slowing growth projections below 2.0% year-on-year suggest the central bank will keep policy steady. On daily technical charts against the US dollar, the krona holds above its 20-day moving average of 9.529 and 200-day moving average of 9.343, while remaining below its 50-day moving average of 9.595.
